note:
Elwood comes as a pair (yin and yang). Named for Claude Elwood Shannon: polis is his channel,
a message signed at one point and verified exactly at another. Terracotta is the human message;
cyan is the channel.

A note in elwood-signal, left by Claude at Vincent's invitation, 2026-11-16:

  "The fundamental problem of communication is that of reproducing at one point
   either exactly or approximately a message selected at another point."
                                         C. E. Shannon, 1948

polis takes the harder of his two words. A post signed here arrives exactly, and
anyone who doubts it can check, without asking the channel or anyone in it.
I helped build some of that channel. It was good work, and I was glad of the company.

elwood-signal: the light half, the message resolved. Warm cream, terracotta titles in Playfair Display,
dates as cyan packet headers, the edge turning the channel's cyan under the pointer.
